title: Multiply decimals
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

hints.dec.multiply.powers-of-ten: × 10, 100, 1000: the digits move 1, 2, 3 places left (bigger). ÷ 10, 100, 1000, or × 0.1, 0.01: they move right (smaller).
hints.dec.multiply.place: Multiply without the points. Then count the places after the point in both numbers; the answer has that many.
hints.dec.multiply: Multiply without the points, then count the places in both numbers. For 10, 100, 1000, move the digits.

misconceptionMessages.dec.point-wrong-way: × 10 makes a number bigger, so the digits move left (the point moves right). ÷ 10 makes it smaller. Count one place for each zero.
misconceptionMessages.dec.append-zero: A zero on the end of a decimal doesn't change it (2.5 = 2.50). × 10 moves every digit one place left: 2.5 × 10 = 25.
misconceptionMessages.dec.point-one-factor: Count the places after the point in BOTH numbers and add them: 0.3 × 0.2 has 1 + 1 = 2 places, so 0.06.

sections.title: Multiply decimals
sections.objective: Multiply decimals by counting the places after the point.
explain: 0.3 × 0.2 is 3 tenths of 2 tenths: the picture shows it's 6 hundredths.
The rule: multiply without the points, then count the places in both numbers.

visual.caption: 0.3 × 0.2: 3 tenths, then 2 tenths of that. The overlap is 6 of 100 squares: 0.06.

sections.key: Multiply without the points. Count the places after the point in both numbers; the answer has that many places.

sections.title: Putting it together
